question: Which instrument was used to measure economic growth during the planning era?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross Domestic Product.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **GDP** became a central measure for assessing economic growth and progress during the** planning era**, helping to evaluate the effectiveness of various Five-Year Plans.
 
• GDP includes the** total** value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders, providing a broad view of economic activity and growth.
 
• While** National Income** was there, **GDP** gained prominence as the standard metric for measuring economic growth, particularly as planning and policy frameworks evolved.
 
• **Economic Planning: **GDP data were crucial for setting economic targets and policy planning, allowing policymakers to track progress and make adjustments to achieve development goals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Per Capita Gross Domestic Product (GDP):**

 
 
• Per Capita GDP is the GDP divided by the population of a country, providing an average economic output per person.
 
• It is used to measure the **economic standard** of living or prosperity of individuals within a country, rather than the total economic output.
 
• Useful for comparing economic performance and living standards between different countries or regions.
 
 
 
• **Per Capita Income:**
 
 
• Per Capita Income is the total income of a country divided by its population, reflecting the average income earned by individuals.
 
• **Economic Indicator:** Provides insight into the average standard of living and economic well-being of the population.
 
• Helps in analyzing** income distribution** and** disparities** within the country.
 
 
 
• **National Income:**
 
 
• National Income is the total value of goods and services produced within a country plus net income from abroad, including wages, rents, and profits.
 
• Used extensively during the** early** planning era for measuring **economic performance** and setting policy targets.
 
• It Includes various components like **Gross National Product (GNP)**, **Net National Product (NNP)**, and **personal income**, providing a broad measure of economic activity.
